title: Multi-Turn Conversational Contexts
hypothesis: Multi-turn conversation fragments produce higher SORC than single-paragraph expert text at matched token count. Conversational structure creates cross-turn relational binding: question tokens and answer tokens across different turns are semantically distinct but relationally linked, generating second-order structure that a single-domain paragraph does not produce.
context_version: v4 (multi_turn: 4-6 turn fragments, same 5 domains, ~200 tokens each)
rationale: ISC's 29 observed instances of differential emergence occurred in extended multi-turn conversations, not single-shot prompts. A multi-turn fragment has structural properties a single paragraph cannot replicate: each turn introduces distinct vocabulary and syntactic role (question vs answer), while the turns are relationally linked through the shared topic. This cross-turn relational binding should increase spectral entropy in the second-order matrix at deep layers relative to a single-paragraph expert context, because the turn-boundary vocabulary shifts prevent the deep-layer semantic clustering that suppressed expert SORC in exp_002 and exp_003.
finding: Multi-turn (195 tok, 0.159) > expert (206 tok, 0.141) at matched token count. 13% higher SORC. Cohen's d = 3.01 (large effect). Late/early layer ratio higher for multi-turn (0.655) than expert (0.626), consistent with cross-turn vocabulary variation preventing full semantic clustering at deep layers. Degenerate < all structured categories holds across all 5 categories. Known confound: Q:/A: markers may drive some token-type diversity independent of relational structure. Requires controlled follow-up with unmarked conversational text.
conclusion: First positive result for ISC conversational prediction. Conversational structure produces measurably higher SORC than single-paragraph expert text at matched token count. The mechanism is consistent with cross-turn relational binding rather than domain-internal semantic clustering. Confound (turn markers) must be isolated in exp_005.
